newsitem.title: FRANCE: Petain admirers demonstrate near his grave.
newsitem.headline: Petain admirers demonstrate near his grave.

text.p: Admirers of Marshal Philippe Petain, head of France's wartime Vichy regime, were turned away on Monday when they sought to enter the now-disused army fortress where he was imprisoned and died after being sentenced for collaboration, officials said.
Some 50 Petain sympathisers tried to enter the fort on the island of Yeu off the French Atlantic coast after laying a wreath at his grave there, the officials said.
Other tributes marking the end of fighting in World War One on November 11, 1918 included flowers from extreme rightist leader Jean-Marie Le Pen.
Similar tributes in the past by the late President Francois Mitterrand were discontinued after they sparked a major row in France.
Petain became a national hero commanding French forces at the 1916 Battle of Verdun. Admirers regularly pay tribute to him on Armistice Day.
He was sentenced to death for collaboration in 1945 but the sentenced was commuted to life imprisonement and he died in 1951.
